sample_size_resolution.round_54_error: The Round 54 simulation used linear Gaussian features with no interactions and no site effects. This made the problem artificially easy — AUC ≈ 0.99 even at n=30. The simulation was measuring whether the algorithm could recover a structure WE ENCODED, not whether the real clinical dataset is powered.
sample_size_resolution.round_55_fix: The new simulation includes: (a) nonlinear interactions (features modulate each other), (b) site heterogeneity (random shifts), (c) variable missingness, (d) false discovery rate estimation. The problem is now substantially harder.
sample_size_resolution.contradiction_resolved: Round 54 claimed both n=100 and n≥500. The corrected simulation shows: REALISTIC scenario requires n≥NOT ACHIEVED in tested range, PESSIMISTIC requires n≥NOT ACHIEVED. The contradiction was caused by the too-easy Round 54 simulation.
sample_size_resolution.honest_recommendation: Use n≥1000 (pessimistic scenario) as the pre-registered minimum. If this is infeasible, the study may not be powered for discovery — consider focusing on Model D (existing data) first.
sample_size_resolution.key_lesson: A sample-size simulation that recovers the structure you encoded is circular. The simulation must be HARDER than the expected reality to be trustworthy.

model_d_existing_data.question: What proportion of the 57% 'recurrence' has NO objective findings (normal ICP, improved papilledema, no restenosis)?
data_sources: 178-patient VSS study (2025): 57% symptomatic recurrence (101/178), average opening pressure fell by 9.6 cm H2O, 75% had papilledema improvement/resolution, 17% required further surgery
Repeat-stenting series: 72.2% had ongoing headaches, only minority (17%) required further surgery

from_178_patient_study.estimated_R2_C1_R2_C2_true_failure: ~30 patients (those requiring surgery have objective pressure failure or restenosis)
from_178_patient_study.estimated_R2_C3_residual_headache: 101 - 30 = ~71 patients have symptomatic recurrence WITHOUT requiring surgery
from_178_patient_study.BUT: Not requiring surgery ≠ no objective findings. Some may have elevated ICP managed medically, or papilledema worsening without surgery. The study does not cleanly separate 'no objective findings' from 'managed without surgery.'

from_repeat_stenting_series.BUT: The series is selected (patients who underwent repeat stenting), so it may over-represent objective findings. The denominator is patients who had repeat stenting, not all VSS patients.

from_178_patient_study_papilledema.papilledema_improvement_resolution: 75% of the FULL cohort had improvement/resolution
from_178_patient_study_papilledema.among_recurrent_patients: The study reports that MANY recurrent patients showed continued ICP reduction and papilledema improvement — but does not report the EXACT proportion
from_178_patient_study_papilledema.source_limitation: The source does NOT cleanly report: 'X% of recurrent patients have ICP ≤ 20 AND improved papilledema AND no restenosis.' This number CANNOT be extracted from the published data without the raw dataset.

model_d_verdict.can_model_d_be_fully_tested_on_existing_: NO — the existing publications do not report the cross-tabulation needed to determine how many recurrent patients have ALL objective measures normal. The raw patient-level data would be needed.

what_CAN_be_inferred.minimum_R2_C3_prevalence: ~55-70% of the 57% recurrence group likely has NO objective pressure failure (inferred from: 17% required surgery, and many recurrent patients had continued ICP/papilledema improvement)
what_CAN_be_inferred.maximum_R2_C3_prevalence: Up to 100% of the non-surgery recurrence group (if ALL of them have normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis)
what_CAN_be_inferred.best_estimate: ~40-50% of ALL VSS patients (70% of 57% = ~40%, adjusted for uncertainty) may have the R2-C3 phenotype
what_CAN_be_inferred.confidence: LOW — inferred from aggregate statistics, not patient-level cross-tabulation

model_d_verdict.what_is_needed_for_definitive_Model_D_te: Access to the raw patient-level data from the 178-patient study to compute: (headache recurrence) AND (ICP ≤ 20) AND (papilledema improved) AND (no restenosis) for each patient.
model_d_verdict.immediate_action: Request raw data access from the 178-patient study investigators. This is the cheapest, fastest path to a definitive Model D test.
model_d_verdict.if_raw_data_unavailable: The best available estimate is ~40-50% R2-C3 prevalence, which is HIGH ENOUGH to justify the prospective study. But the uncertainty means the study must include robust endpoint validation.

model_d_existing_data.model_d_conclusion: Model D is NOT fully falsifiable on existing published data. The raw patient-level data is needed. The best available estimate suggests R2-C3 prevalence is ~40-50% — high enough to justify continued investigation but with LOW confidence. The immediate action is to request raw data access.

ICP_threshold.source: International Headache Society classification (ICHD-3) defines normal ICP as ≤ 20 cm H2O in adults. This is the standard clinical threshold used in IIH diagnostic criteria (Modified Dandy Criteria).
ICP_threshold.provenance: ICHD-3 (2018, International Headache Society); Modified Dandy Criteria (original IIH diagnostic criteria)
ICP_threshold.limitation: ICP measured via lumbar puncture (opening pressure) is a SINGLE TIMEPOINT measurement. ICP varies with posture, respiration, and time. A normal LP pressure does NOT guarantee normal ICP at all times. The threshold is a CLINICAL CONVENTION, not a physiological ground truth.

HIT_6_threshold.source: Headache Impact Test-6 (HIT-6) validated instrument. Score ≥ 50 = 'severe impact' (the highest category). This threshold is widely used in headache clinical trials as a meaningful clinical endpoint.
HIT_6_threshold.provenance: Bayliss MS et al. (2003) HIT-6 validation; used in FDA headache trial endpoints
HIT_6_threshold.limitation: HIT-6 measures HEADACHE IMPACT, not headache frequency or IIH-specific symptoms. A patient with severe migraine (not IIH) would also score ≥ 50. The threshold captures 'clinically significant headache' but does NOT confirm IIH-related headache.
HIT_6_threshold.important_note: This is exactly why Model D (artifact) is important — HIT-6 ≥ 50 may capture non-IIH headache. The endpoint must be COMBINED with normalized ICP and papilledema to narrow to the R2-C3 phenotype.

papilledema_improvement.source: Frisén papilledema grading scale (standardized, validated). Improvement ≥ 1 grade is considered clinically meaningful.
papilledema_improvement.provenance: Frisén L (1982) original grading scale; modified by various IIH studies
papilledema_improvement.limitation: Frisén grading is SUBJECTIVE (observer-dependent). Requires certified graders. Inter-observer variability is ~1 grade. The threshold 'improvement ≥ 1' is at the edge of measurement variability.
papilledema_improvement.mitigation: Use photographic grading by central reading center with ≥2 independent graders (machine-gradable in future with AI fundus image analysis)

no_restenosis.threshold: No imaging-confirmed in-stent or adjacent stenosis on MRV/CTV/DSA at 12 months
no_restenosis.source: Standard VSS follow-up imaging protocol. Stenosis defined as >50% luminal narrowing on angiography.
no_restenosis.provenance: VSS clinical practice; >50% threshold from vascular stenting literature
no_restenosis.limitation: MRV has limited sensitivity for in-stent restenosis (metal artifact). CTV is better but still imperfect. DSA is gold standard but invasive. The imaging modality matters — different sites may use different modalities.
no_restenosis.mitigation: Standardize imaging modality across sites (CTV or DSA, not MRV for in-stent assessment)

confounding_framework.OLD_approach_REMOVED: Simple permutation of labels — INCORRECT because it ignores causal structure. Permuting site labels ignores that site encodes real population/technique differences. Regressing out BMI may destroy a real biological mediation.

NEW_approach.name: Site-stratified validation
NEW_approach.method: Perform discovery WITHIN each site separately. If the same phenotype structure appears in ≥2/3 sites, it is not a site artifact. This is STRONGER than permutation because it tests REPLICATION across sites.
NEW_approach.addresses: Site effects, population differences, measurement protocol variations

NEW_approach.name: Leave-one-site-out validation
NEW_approach.method: Train discovery model on all sites except one. Test on the held-out site. If the phenotype structure replicates, it generalizes across sites.

NEW_approach.name: Stent-stratified analysis
NEW_approach.method: Perform discovery separately for each stent type. If the same phenotype appears across stent types, it is not a stent artifact.

NEW_approach.name: Causal mediation analysis (BMI)
NEW_approach.method: Use causal mediation analysis (not simple regression) to determine: (a) does BMI affect the phenotype directly, (b) does BMI affect the phenotype through venous physiology (mediation), (c) what is the natural direct effect vs natural indirect effect? This DISTINGUISHES 'BMI is a confounder' from 'BMI is a mediator' — the latter means the phenotype is REAL and BMI is part of the causal chain.
NEW_approach.addresses: BMI confounding vs mediation — the key distinction the CEO identified

NEW_approach.name: Negative controls
NEW_approach.method: Test whether the phenotype predicts outcomes it SHOULD NOT predict (e.g., age, sex, unrelated comorbidities). If it does, the phenotype is capturing general health status, not IIH-specific physiology.

NEW_approach.name: Measurement-error stress test
NEW_approach.method: Add known amounts of noise to each signal and re-run discovery. If the phenotype structure collapses under realistic measurement error, it is not robust enough for clinical use.

NEW_approach.name: Time-shifted analysis
NEW_approach.method: Use baseline features to predict 12-month outcome, and separately use 12-month features to predict baseline (reverse causation test). If 12-month features predict baseline, the model has reverse causation bias.

decision_value_gate.the_problem: The Round 54 decision-value test compared AI recommendation vs 'standard care' — but who defines standard care? If AI-generated, the loop risks comparing AI vs AI and discovering its own usefulness.
decision_value_gate.the_fix: Freeze an EXTERNAL, SOURCE-BOUND standard-of-care decision policy BEFORE running the phenotype discovery. This policy is derived from published guidelines, not generated by the machine.

frozen_standard_care_policy.source: Published IIH treatment guidelines + VSS clinical practice
policy: IF headache persists after VSS → check ICP via lumbar puncture
IF ICP elevated → consider repeat VSS or shunt surgery
IF ICP normal → consider medication adjustment (acetazolamide, topiramate)
IF headache persists despite normal ICP and medication adjustment → refer to headache specialist
IF visual symptoms worsen → urgent neuro-ophthalmology referral
frozen_standard_care_policy.frozen_date: 2026-08-21 (pre-registered, cannot be modified after phenotype discovery)

the_test.design: For each patient in the validation cohort: (a) apply the FROZEN standard care policy → standard_recommendation, (b) apply the phenotype-guided policy → phenotype_recommendation, (c) compare
the_test.success_criterion: Phenotype-guided recommendation DIFFERS from frozen standard care in ≥30% of cases AND the difference maps to a real, existing intervention
the_test.failure_criterion: If phenotype-guided = frozen standard in ≥70% of cases → phenotype does not change decisions → NOT an invention
the_test.key_safeguard: The frozen standard care policy CANNOT be modified after phenotype discovery. This prevents the machine from redefining 'standard care' to make the phenotype look useful.

phenotype_guided_policy.note: This policy is NOT frozen — it depends on the discovered phenotype. But it must map to EXISTING interventions (not invented ones).
interventions: venous_phenotype → consider venous intervention (repeat VSS, CPAP if OSA-related)
migraine_phenotype → CGRP antagonist trial, migraine prophylaxis
artifact_phenotype → reclassify, refer to headache specialist (no IIH escalation)

what_was_fixed: 1. Sample-size: circular simulation replaced with sensitivity grid (nonlinear + site effects + FDR). Contradiction resolved.

2. Model D: tested on existing data — CANNOT be fully resolved from published data (raw patient-level data needed). Best estimate: ~40-50% R2-C3 prevalence, LOW confidence. Immediate action: request raw data.
3. Endpoints: all 4 thresholds source-bound (ICHD-3, HIT-6 validation, Frisén scale, VSS imaging protocol). Limitations acknowledged.
4. Confounding: simple permutation REPLACED with causal framework (site-stratified, leave-one-site-out, causal mediation for BMI, negative controls, measurement-error stress, time-shifted analysis).
5. Decision-value: frozen external standard-care policy (source-bound from published guidelines). Cannot be modified after discovery. Prevents AI-vs-AI comparison.
immediate_next_steps: 1. Request raw patient-level data from the 178-patient VSS study investigators for definitive Model D test
2. If raw data unavailable, use best estimate (~40-50% R2-C3 prevalence) for sample-size calculation
3. Finalize sample size using the pessimistic scenario from the sensitivity grid
4. Initiate IRB for prospective study with corrected architecture
5. Do NOT generate mechanism until discovery + decision-value both succeed
verdict.gate_status: YELLOW — architecture is corrected, but Model D is not definitively resolved (raw data needed) and sample size is not finalized (depends on Model D prevalence estimate)
